concepts.name: Origin and Founding of Chalukyas of Badami
key_dimensions: Disputed theories of origin: indigenous Kannada clan vs. immigrant Gurjara/Rajput lineage
Role of Pulakesi I as founder and the Vatapi/Badami capital establishment (~543 CE)
Relationship with the Kadamba dynasty and early territorial consolidation
UPSC Trap: Distinguishing Chalukyas of Badami from Chalukyas of Kalyani and Vengi branch

concepts.name: Pulakesi II: Military Campaigns and Political Significance
key_dimensions: Defeat of Harshavardhana at the Battle of Narmada (~618-619 CE) — significance as the only major check on Harsha
Campaigns against Pallavas, Kadambas, Gangas, and Mauryas of Konkan
Aihole Prashasti by Ravikirti as a primary source — its literary and historical value
Diplomatic exchange with Persian emperor Khusrau II (Chosroes II) — Ajanta Cave painting evidence
UPSC Trap: Pulakesi II was defeated and killed by Pallava king Narasimhavarman I (not Mahendravarman)

concepts.name: Aihole Prashasti: Content, Authorship, and Historical Significance
key_dimensions: Authored by court poet Ravikirti — composed in Sanskrit, inscribed at Meguti Temple, Aihole
Content: eulogizes Pulakesi II, mentions defeat of Harsha, compares Ravikirti to Kalidasa and Bharavi
Significance as a primary source for dating and military history of Pulakesi II's reign
UPSC Trap: Aihole Prashasti is different from the Badami Cave inscriptions of Mangalesa

concepts.name: Chalukya-Pallava Conflict: Causes, Phases, and Consequences
key_dimensions: Three-phase rivalry spanning nearly a century — control over Vengi and Deccan supremacy
Pulakesi II's early success vs. Narasimhavarman I's capture of Vatapi (~642 CE) and death of Pulakesi II
Revival under Vikramaditya I who recaptured Vatapi from Pallavas
Impact on art: cross-pollination between Chalukyan and Pallava architectural styles
UPSC Trap: Narasimhavarman I took the title 'Vatapikonda' to commemorate victory over Vatapi

concepts.name: Vikramaditya I and II: Consolidation and Cultural Patronage
key_dimensions: Vikramaditya I's role in reversing Pallava gains and restoring Chalukya prestige
Vikramaditya II's repeated invasions of Pallava capital Kanchipuram — notable for sparing the city
Patronage of Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal by Vikramaditya II's queen Lokamahadevi
UPSC Trap: Pattadakal temples were built under Vikramaditya II, not Pulakesi II

concepts.name: Kirtivarman I and Mangalesa: Succession and Internal Conflict
key_dimensions: Kirtivarman I's military expansion against Nalas, Mauryas of Konkan, and Kadambas
Mangalesa as regent who usurped throne from Kirtivarman I's son Pulakesi II — dynastic conflict
Badami Cave inscriptions as primary source for Mangalesa's reign
UPSC Trap: Pulakesi II had to fight his own uncle Mangalesa to reclaim the throne

concepts.name: Administrative System of Chalukyas of Badami
key_dimensions: Feudatory system: kingdom divided into Rashtra (province), Vishaya (district), and Grama (village)
Role of Mahasamantas and Maharajas as feudal vassals — semi-independent nature
Revenue system: land grants (agraharas) to Brahmanas, devadana to temples
Role of village assemblies (Mahajanas) — continuity with earlier South Indian traditions
UPSC Trap: Chalukyan administration shows transition from centralized Gupta model to feudal Deccan polity

concepts.name: Chalukyan Architecture: Badami Cave Temples
key_dimensions: Four rock-cut caves at Badami: Caves 1-3 (Hindu — Shaiva, Vaishnava) and Cave 4 (Jain)
Iconographic program: Cave 1 has Nataraja relief; Cave 3 has Trivikrama and Varaha panels — dated 578 CE (earliest dated Chalukyan monument)
Synthesis of Nagara and Dravida elements in early Chalukyan style
UPSC Trap: Cave 3 at Badami has a dedicatory inscription of Mangalesa, making it the earliest dated cave

concepts.name: Chalukyan Architecture: Structural Temples and the Vesara Style
key_dimensions: Pattadakal as the culmination — UNESCO World Heritage Site with 10 temples mixing Nagara and Dravida
Virupaksha Temple and Mallikarjuna Temple (Dravida) vs. Papanatha Temple (Nagara) at Pattadakal
Vesara style: hybrid style formally associated with Chalukyas — contested definition (Ferguson vs. others)
Aihole as the 'laboratory of Indian architecture' — over 70 temples including Lad Khan Temple and Durga Temple
UPSC Trap: Durga Temple at Aihole is NOT dedicated to goddess Durga — name derived from 'durg' (fort)

concepts.name: Lad Khan Temple and Durga Temple at Aihole: Architectural Features
key_dimensions: Lad Khan Temple: flat-roofed, early Chalukyan style, originally a community hall — one of the earliest structural Hindu temples
Durga Temple: apsidal plan with a semi-circular apse, gallery circumambulation — unique in Indian temple architecture
Durga Temple's shikhara represents early Nagara development in the Deccan
UPSC Trap: Lad Khan Temple's flat roof and pillared hall resemble Buddhist viharas — shows Buddhist influence on early Hindu temples

concepts.name: Religion and Patronage under Chalukyas of Badami
key_dimensions: Primary patronage of Shaivism — Pulakesi I performed Ashwamedha and Hiranyagarbha rituals
Simultaneous patronage of Vaishnavism and Jainism — religious eclecticism as a political tool
Role of Brahmanas: land grants (agraharas) as instruments of Brahmanization of the Deccan
UPSC Trap: Despite Shaiva leanings, Pulakesi II's court poet Ravikirti was a Jain — demonstrates pluralism

concepts.name: Chinese Pilgrim Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) and the Chalukyan Court
key_dimensions: Xuanzang visited the Deccan around 641 CE — provides external corroboration for Pulakesi II's reign
Description of Pulakesi II as a powerful king with a large army including war elephants
Xuanzang's account as a cross-reference with the Aihole Prashasti for chronology
UPSC Trap: Xuanzang visited the Chalukyan kingdom BEFORE Pulakesi II's defeat by Narasimhavarman I

concepts.name: Vengi Branch (Eastern Chalukyas): Origin and Significance
key_dimensions: Founded by Kubja Vishnuvardhana, brother of Pulakesi II — established kingdom in coastal Andhra
Long-lasting dynasty (7th–12th century) as a distinct branch from Badami
Later alliance with Cholas through matrimonial alliances — led to Chalukya-Chola dynasty
UPSC Trap: Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi are NOT the same as Chalukyas of Kalyani (Western Chalukyas)

concepts.name: Decline of Chalukyas of Badami and Rise of Rashtrakutas
key_dimensions: Last significant ruler: Kirtivarman II — overthrown by Dantidurga (Rashtrakuta) around 753–755 CE
Internal feudatory rebellions as a primary cause of decline
Rashtrakutas' rise as former feudatories of Chalukyas — significance for understanding feudalism
UPSC Trap: After Chalukyas of Badami, it is the Rashtrakutas (not Chalukyas of Kalyani) who dominate — Kalyani Chalukyas revived LATER in 973 CE

concepts.name: Economy and Trade under Chalukyas of Badami
key_dimensions: Control over Deccan trade routes connecting North India and South India — strategic importance of Badami location
Agricultural economy supported by tank irrigation — early evidence in Karnataka region
Maritime trade through Konkan ports — campaigns against Mauryas of Konkan for port control
UPSC Trap: The Chalukyan economy was transitioning from a monetized economy (Gupta period) to a land-grant-based feudal economy

concepts.name: Literature and Language under Chalukyas of Badami
key_dimensions: Official language: Sanskrit for inscriptions (Aihole Prashasti) but Kannada also used
Earliest Kannada inscriptions associated with the Chalukyan period — significance for Kannada linguistic history
Court poets: Ravikirti (Sanskrit); patronage of both Sanskrit and Prakrit literature
UPSC Trap: Kannada literature's early development is often attributed to Chalukyas, but the Halmidi inscription (oldest Kannada) predates the Chalukyas slightly — associated with Kadambas

concepts.name: Pattadakal Temple Complex: Political and Religious Symbolism
key_dimensions: Served as coronation site for Chalukyan kings — political-religious significance
Built by multiple queens and kings — Lokamahadevi (Virupaksha), Trailokyamahadevi (Mallikarjuna), suggesting queen agency
Represents the matured Chalukyan synthesis — influenced by Pallava Kanchipuram architecture
UNESCO recognition and UPSC frequently links Pattadakal with the Vesara style debate

concepts.name: Chalukyas and the Ashwamedha Tradition: Political Legitimacy
key_dimensions: Pulakesi I performed Ashwamedha and Hiranyagarbha rituals to establish Kshatriya legitimacy
Significance: demonstrates Brahmanical legitimization strategy for a newly emerging dynasty
Parallels with other post-Gupta kingdoms (Pushyabhutis, Pallavas) using similar strategies
UPSC Trap: Hiranyagarbha (golden womb ritual) was specifically used to claim Kshatriya status — different from Ashwamedha which claimed overlordship

concepts.name: Sculptural Art of Chalukyas: Iconographic Programs
key_dimensions: Badami Cave sculptures: Harihara, Ardhanarishvara, Varaha, Trivikrama — theological syncretism in visual form
Influence of Gupta sculptural traditions modified by Deccan sensibilities — transition style
Nataraja at Badami Cave 1 — one of the earliest representations of dancing Shiva in South India
UPSC Trap: Chalukyan sculpture shows BOTH Gupta influence (in form) and proto-Dravidian elements (in iconography) — it is a transitional corpus
